literal: Those who were ruined because of negligence, let them think of, when they themselves experience infatuation because of their own joy.
translation: Let people think of those who were ruined by negligence, at the very moment they find themselves infatuated with their own joy.
modern: தங்கள் மகிழ்ச்சியினால் செருக்குற்று மயங்கும் காலத்தில், மறதியினால் (அலட்சியத்தினால்) அழிந்து போனவர்களை நினைத்துப் பார்க்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the danger of complacency that arises from excessive happiness or success. When people are overjoyed, they often lose their vigilance and become infatuated or prideful ('மைந்துறும்'). To prevent the ruin that follows such negligence ('இகழ்ச்சி'), the poet advises them to remember those who were once prosperous but got ruined because they let their guard down. Reflecting on the downfall of others serves as a powerful reality check to maintain mindfulness.
